title: hax
brief: A minimalist coding agent that runs natively in the terminal. The "minimalist" claim comes from the sharer's one-line description and is unverified.
caveat: The "minimalist" claim comes from the sharer's one-line description and is unverified.
details: hax (usehax.dev, OleksandrChekhovskyi/hax) — a minimalist, terminal-native coding agent: a single native C binary with a small dependency set that starts instantly and uses only a few MB of memory — leaving more RAM for local models. Local models are first-class (`hax --provider llama.cpp` auto-discovers the model, no provider config block needed); broad provider support otherwise (OpenAI + compatible, Anthropic + compatible, Codex via ChatGPT subscription, OpenRouter, OpenCode Zen/Go…). It respects your terminal: streaming Markdown and live tool output reflowed, only the current line redrawn, native scrollback preserved, never a full-screen takeover. Inspectable via a transcript view (Ctrl+T) and optional wire-protocol traces. Well-behaved Unix tooling: XDG paths, clean stdout in `-p` one-shot mode with resume hints on stderr, plain-text config/session files, composition via subprocesses instead of plugins — and a philosophy doc explaining each deliberate omission (no MCP marketplaces, plugin runtime, IDE panels, or per-command permission prompts). Homebrew tap, AUR, static Linux binaries, builds on Linux/macOS/FreeBSD/OpenBSD (Windows via WSL).
